name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch (Wall Drill)
description: Improves ankle mobility to prevent calf strains and knee injuries.
steps: Stand facing a wall with one foot forward.
Keep your heel on the ground.
Drive your knee forward toward the wall.
Hold for 2 seconds and return.
mistakes: Lifting the heel off the ground.

name: Box Breathing Recovery
description: Regulates the nervous system to accelerate recovery and reduce cortisol.
steps: Inhale deeply for 4 seconds.
Hold your breath for 4 seconds.
Exhale slowly for 4 seconds.
Hold empty for 4 seconds.

name: Weighted Calf Raises
description: Strengthens the lower leg to prevent Achilles tendonitis and ankle sprains.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Slowly push up onto the balls of your feet.
Pause at the top and squeeze the calf.
Lower back down with control.

name: Copenhagen Plank
description: The gold standard for groin (adductor) injury prevention.
steps: Place top foot on a bench in a side plank position.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Bring the bottom leg up to meet the bench.
Hold for the prescribed duration.
mistakes: Pushing through the knee instead of the foot.

name: Lower Body Foam Rolling
description: Myofascial release to reduce muscle soreness and improve blood flow.
steps: Place the roller under the target muscle (Quads/Hamstrings).
Slowly roll back and forth over the muscle.
Pause on tight spots for 20-30 seconds.
Maintain steady breathing throughout.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Activates the posterior chain to protect the lower back and knees.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Form a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower slowly and repeat.
mistakes: Pushing through the toes instead of heels.

name: Dynamic Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Opens up the hips to improve sprint mechanics and reduce back pain.
steps: Kneel on one knee in a lunge position.
Tuck your pelvis under (posterior tilt).
Lean forward slightly until you feel a stretch in the thigh.
Reach the same-side arm overhead for an intensified stretch.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward without pelvic control.

name: 90/90 Hip Rotation
description: Enhances internal and external hip rotation for better multi-directional speed.
steps: Sit on the floor with both knees bent at 90 degrees.
Ensure one leg is in front and one is to the side.
Rotate your torso over the front leg.
Switch sides without using your hands if possible.
mistakes: Forcing the movement past comfort range.

name: Dynamic Leg Swings (Front/Side)
description: Increases blood flow and dynamic range of motion in the posterior chain.
steps: Hold onto a stable surface for balance.
Swing one leg forward and backward with control.
Switch to side-to-side swings across the body.
Gradually increase the range of motion.
mistakes: Moving the torso instead of the hip.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: The #1 exercise for reducing hamstring strain risk in sprinters.
steps: Kneel on a soft surface with ankles secured by a partner or rack.
Lower your torso toward the ground as slowly as possible.
Keep your hips extended and body straight.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up.
mistakes: Bending at the hips (breaking the line).

name: Romanian Deadlift (RPE 6-7)
description: Builds posterior chain strength to protect the hamstrings and lower back.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width, holding weights in front.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping legs straight.
Lower the weights until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Squeeze glutes to return to standing.
mistakes: Keeping the weights too far from the body.

name: Scapular Push-Up
description: Improves shoulder blade stability to prevent upper body impingements.
steps: Start in a high plank position.
Without bending your elbows, sink your chest down.
Push back up by protracting your shoulder blades.
Maintain a tight core throughout.

name: Single-Leg Squat (Control-focused)
description: Essential for knee stability and lateral movement control (ACL protection).
steps: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward.
Lower your hips back and down with control.
Ensure the knee stays aligned over the toes.
Push through the heel to return to start.
mistakes: Letting the heel lift off the ground.
